description.narrative:
The aim of the project is to increase awareness and access to cervical cancer screening among sex workers in Ntoroko District. Ntoroko District is mainly occupied by the minority tribe of Batuku. Sex workers in this area, although engaging in activities that transmit HPV (causative agent of cervical cancer), continue to lack knowledge and service points for cervical cancer related services. Moreover cervical cancer contributes 40% of all cancers recorded among women in Uganda. This is as a result of limited access to screening. The Batuku Community in Ntoroko like all other minority groups, have been neglected in the areas of health and education. This has created a serious knowledge gap when it comes to areas of cancer screening. Although cancer screening exists in some facilities, they are never accessed by batuku sex workers. Our project will aim at bridging the knowledge gap that exists among sex workers in this community as regards to these two cancers. We also aim to ensure that by the end of theproject, all sex workers will be equipped with knowledge about these two cancers and where to seek help whenever they are suspicious. We shall demystify the current idea that cancer is a death sentence. We also want to arrest any cancers during the project period before they become advanced through cancer screening camps in this target population. During the course of this project, our survivors will also be given a boost in the financial aspect. KHIWE plans to empower the ladies with skills in differentsectors so that they can support themselves. The areas identified by KHIWE are: • Tailoring, • Baking, • Making of liquid soap. • Rearing of animals. • Crafts • Fishing • Growing of crops
To make sure that these women are off to a good start,KHIWE will reach out to possible clients such as schools, hospitals, restaurants and local government offices to create market. Training will be conducted in groups of 5-10 women for a period of 4 weeks. This training will not only cover what they are supposed to do but also how to do business in general. After the trainings are done, KHIWEwill equip each one of them with seed capital to go out and start, there will be follow up from KHIWE to see how they are doing andrender support in any areas theywill be finding issues with. KHIWE will make it a point to make sure that these women elevate theirlives in every way possible based on how their businesses are doing. In this, KHIWE is looking at the women affording better healthcare, taking their children to better schools, creating savings groups and being able to save in their groups on a weekly basis. Overall, KHIWE’s aim is to make sure that the women have improved their standards of living.

participating-org.narrative:
Kabarole Hospital Initiative on Women Under Exploitation( KHIWE) was established in 2017. This initiative arose out of the rampant numbers of women who would come to the hospital seeking medical attention as a result of diseases and injuries sustained in their line of work. Such people included women under Gender Based violence, survivors of rape and assault, marginalized LGBTQ. The organization is composed of 7 members( 4 from community/rightsholders and 3 from Hospital). These individuals started by sitting quarterly in2017 to brainstorm on how best to help women under exploitation in the Rwenzori region. A constitution governing the group was developed and adopted in 2018 where the group registered as a Community Based Organization. The organization ensures that from Board level to management and operations, at least a third of the positions are filled by women/rightsholders. The groups uses contributions from members to assist these women through paying Hospital bills and other small empowerment acts like counselling. The group members also volunteer their time to work with these survivors of GBV in areas of medical and economic empowerment. The idea of applying for grants came later in 2021, otherwise all the activities have been funded from member contributions. The group also hopes to formally register as an independent NGO in future.
OBJECTIVES
• To Identify, and rescue women and girls who are victims of sexual exploitation and abuse • To Fight all forms of sex trafficking in Ruwenzori and surrounding areas, offer timely interventions to save lives • To Improve abused girls and women’s access to legal redress through partnerships with existing justice systems • To providing survivors with legal representation, social services, and temporary shelter • To Empower rescued women and girls with 21st Century livelihoods skills to improve their employability and profitability • To build capacity through trainings of both clients and willing women and girls to manage their businesses efficiently and sustainably • To lessen the proportion of women and girls living in extreme poverty in Ruwenzori through planned collective work
